text: This story contains one of the Bible's hardest commands. God tells Saul to destroy the Amalekites completely, including women, children and infants (1 Samuel 15:3), and the Bible says that Saul did, apart from King Agag and the best of the animals. The game does not show or describe the fighting. It gives God's command in the Bible's own words, says that the Amalekites were devoted to destruction, and then follows the story's real subject: Saul's disobedience.
The Bible also says that Samuel later put King Agag to death (15:33). The game does not include this.

The device hums. A camp on the edge of the desert, at Gilgal, near the place where the Israelites first entered the land. King Saul is here, with a huge army. Samuel the prophet, who is very old now, has just walked in from Ramah, and he does not look happy.

text: The LORD is on our side. I have no doubt.
Then Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people Israel. Now therefore, listen to the words of the LORD.
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘I witnessed what the Amalekites did to the Israelites when they opposed them on their way up from Egypt.
Now go and attack the Amalekites and devote to destruction all that belongs to them. Do not spare them, but put to death men and women, children and infants, oxen and sheep, camels and donkeys.’”

You do not understand it, and Samuel does not explain it. The Amalekites attacked the weakest of the Israelites when they came out of Egypt, and they have been enemies ever since. This is the LORD's judgment, and Saul is told to carry it out in full.

Saul and his men kept everything that was good and destroyed what was left. Their obedience was only for the things they did not want.
Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,

speaker: The LORD
text: I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following Me and has not carried out My instructions.
And Samuel was distressed and cried out to the LORD all that night.
Early in the morning Samuel got up to confront Saul, but he was told, “Saul has gone to Carmel, and behold, he has set up a monument for himself and has turned and gone down to Gilgal.”
A tall stone monument, still with fresh chisel marks. Saul put it up for himself.
Saul was the king, and he set up a monument for himself. He was not a bad man, but success was going to his head. He was beginning to think of himself first.
When Samuel reached him, Saul said to him, “May the LORD bless you. I have carried out the LORD’s instructions.”

speaker: Samuel
text: Then what is this bleating of sheep and lowing of cattle that I hear?

speaker: Saul
text: The troops brought them from the Amalekites; they spared the best sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God, but the rest we devoted to destruction.
“Stop!” exclaimed Samuel. “Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.” “Tell me,” Saul replied.

speaker: Samuel
text: Although you were once small in your own eyes, have you not become the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel and sent you on a mission, saying, ‘Go and devote to destruction the sinful Amalekites. Fight against them until you have wiped them out.’

speaker: Samuel
text: So why did you not obey the LORD? Why did you rush upon the plunder and do evil in the sight of the LORD?

speaker: Saul
text: But I did obey the LORD, | I went on the mission that the LORD gave me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek and devoted the Amalekites to destruction. The troops took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of the things devoted to destruction, in order to sacrifice them to the LORD your God at Gilgal.

speaker: Samuel
text: Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness is better than the fat of rams.

speaker: Samuel
text: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and arrogance is like the wickedness of idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has rejected you as king.

speaker: Saul
text: I have sinned; I have transgressed the LORD’s commandment and your instructions, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice. Now therefore, please forgive my sin and return with me so I can worship the LORD.

“I will not return with you,” Samuel replied. “For you have rejected the word of the LORD, and He has rejected you as king over Israel.” As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the hem of his robe, and it tore.

speaker: Samuel
text: The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you. Moreover, the Glory of Israel does not lie or change His mind, for He is not a man, that He should change His mind.

speaker: Saul
text: I have sinned, | Please honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel. Come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD your God.
Long after, Jesus quoted the prophet Hosea about the same thing, when some people asked why He ate with sinners:

speaker: Jesus
text: But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.
So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.

Then Samuel went to Ramah, but Saul went up to his home in Gibeah of Saul. And to the day of his death, Samuel never again visited Saul. Samuel mourned for Saul, and the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.

text: How long are you going to mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.
